name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican fundraising dominance ($2.1M plus $1.3M outside support vs $31K for the Democrat)
Prediction markets price the GOP at 99%
Open seat with no incumbent penalty or boost
model.rationale: TX-19's R+25 lean makes this a Republican stronghold, and the open seat does not change that. Tom Sell has raised over $2.1 million with heavy outside backing, while Kyle Rable has raised about $31,000, and markets price the race at 99% Republican.
model.watch: A polling surprise or major scandal involving the Republican nominee is the only plausible path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
West Texas's 19th District is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+25. Representative Jodey Arrington is retiring, but the seat remains firmly in the GOP column. Tom Sell, the Republican nominee, has raised over $2.1 million and benefits from roughly $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $31,000 with minimal cash on hand.

Prediction markets give the Republican a 99% chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. There are no public general-election polls, but the fundamentals leave little doubt. The forecast expects a Republican win by roughly twenty-plus points, consistent with the district's baseline lean and the lopsided resource gap between the two nominees.
